name: Xamtanga
confidence_why: Reinisch 1884 (Seqot'a variety), Appleyard 1987a (Ziquala and Sehale, as reported in Teshome 2015) and Darmon 2015 (Abɨrgälle and Saqʷät'ä, as reported in Mous 2021) all describe one word accent on the last or second-last syllable, mostly the penult, but they disagree on what places it (vowel quantity, morphology, or a penult default) and Teshome 2015 found no accent in his S'agibji data, so the existence and two-syllable window of word stress are reasonably secure while the placement rule is not.

catalog_quote: 4) Der Accent. 83) Da die Abessinier ähnlich den romanischen Völkern im Allgemeinen die Stimme nur wenig moduliren, so war es mir beim Niederschreiben meiner Texte und Sätze nach dem Dictat meiner Lehrer oft nicht leicht, sofort die richtige Ton- stelle aufzufassen, und bei der Revision meiner Texte finde ich daher nicht selten verschiedene Accentbezeichnungen an ein und demselben Worte ... Im Allgemeinen können jedoch hinsichtlich des Accen- tes folgende Normen zur Richtschnur dienen : a) Der Hauptaccent geht nie auf die drittletzte Silbe zu- rück, sondern ruht auf der letzten oder vorletzten Silbe. b) Bei zweisilbigen Wörtern ruht der Accent auf der letzten Silbe, wenn der Vocal derselben an Quantität den der vorangehenden Silbe überwiegt; z. sweep_summary: Xamtanga (xamt1239) is in the catalog as 'descriptions disagree' (Reinisch 1884 quantity-driven final/penult accent vs Teshome 2015 'accent not attested' vs Appleyard 1987a morphological accent). this search of works with stress in the title had one item, Langus et al. 2012 (JML), which Glottolog's own.bib record shows is a computerized mis-assignment (language code from the title word 'discover', description type from 'structure'); it is a closed-access psycholinguistics paper with no bearing on Xamtanga and should be dropped from the language's bibliography. Beyond the item list, Mous 2021 (already held by the project, read) carries Darmon 2015:33 - one obligatory primary accent per lexical word, mostly penultimate - which refines the conflict record but is second-hand and does not supersede Reinisch. Darmon 2015 (no open copy; HAL notice only) is the high-priority acquisition; Appleyard 1987a (Cambridge, paywalled, re-checked) is medium. Records saved and. for the session was exhausted; only direct downloads were possible.

new_statements.reading: Xamtanga has obligatory culminative word stress (exactly one primary accent per lexical word), predominantly penultimate. This is a second-hand report of Darmon 2015 (first-hand fieldwork), not a first-hand statement itself; the only works with stress in the title (Langus et al. 2012) was a Glottolog computerized mis-assignment and contains nothing on Xamtanga. The Mous/Darmon line supports the existence of word accent against Teshome 2015's footnote and gives a positional generalisation (mostly penult) that neither confirms Reinisch's quantity-driven final/penult rule nor Appleyard's morphological accent; the catalog's 'descriptions disagree' classification stands, with Darmon 2015 as the source that would resolve it.

readall_conflicts: No new source was opened, so no new disagreement arises. The standing conflict recorded in the existing statement remains: the second-hand Darmon 2015:33 report (via Mous 2021 p.4: one culminative primary accent per lexical word, mostly penultimate) versus Reinisch's quantity-driven final/penult rule, Appleyard's morphological accent, and Teshome 2015's footnote doubting word accent; Darmon 2015 is the source that would resolve it and it is not openly available.

sources.quote: Among the Agaw or Central Cushitic languages, Xamtanga is a stress language as it has one and only one primary accent per lexical word which falls mostly on the penultimate syllable (Darmon 2015: 33). In the other Central Cushitic languages, however, obligatoriness is not clearly attested.
sources.locator: p.4 (printed running head '4 Mous'), section on stress languages, paragraph 'A number of Cushitic languages obey the criteria of stress languages'
sources.note: Second-hand (Mous carrying Darmon 2015:33): Xamtanga has obligatory, culminative word stress - exactly one primary accent per lexical word - falling mostly on the penult. Refines the catalog's 'descriptions disagree' record: it sides against Teshome 2015 fn.5 (accent not attested) on the existence of word accent, and gives a positional statement ('mostly penultimate') that differs from Reinisch 1884's quantity-driven final/penult rule and from Appleyard's 'largely a question of morphology'. Not first-hand, one sentence; Darmon 2015 itself remains unopened.

tone.quote: L' indebolimento va anche oltre, e la a perviene ad attenuarsi in i, fino in casi in cui ne' vocaboli tigrai essa sopporta l'accento: ty. marda « collana » khmt. mirdà, ty. nùlà « cervello » khmt. nilà ... Talfiata, poi, la a, anche tonica, addirittura sparisce ... Le altre vocali, in genere, non danno luogo a importanti osservazioni: è soltanto a notarsi la loro caduta, anche se reggenti l'accento, come per una specie di tendenza abbreviatrice del hamta
tone.translation: The weakening goes even further, and a comes to be attenuated to i, even in cases where in the Tigrinya words it bears the accent: Tig. marda 'necklace' Khamta mirdà, Tig. nùlà 'brain' Khamta nilà ... Sometimes, moreover, a, even when tonic (stressed), disappears altogether ... The other vowels, in general, give no occasion for important observations: one need only note their loss, even when they carry the accent, as by a kind of abbreviating tendency of Khamta
